scene.note: Your scripts read the logger's year of readings a line at a time and keep only their totals, so they fit in the little memory of the box by the tap.

steps.note: All year the logger writes a line every minute for each tap, so the log grows far bigger than the box's memory.
A read stream takes the log in small pieces, and readline joins them back into whole lines.
count-readings.js gets one line at a time and adds one for each reading. Blank lines and notes do not count.
When the log ends, Imran gets the number of readings, and the script never held more than a line.
The log comes through a line at a time, as before.
water-year.js takes the litres from the end of each reading and adds them to its total.
Imran gets one line: the litres of the whole log, added up.
tap-totals.js reads each line's tap and its litres.
It keeps one running total for each tap it has seen, never the lines themselves.
Imran gets a line for each tap, in the order of their names, and can see which tap uses the most.
